answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with quadratic identity pricing: the first identity is cheap, but each additional one funded from the same source costs quadratically more — the tenth costs a hundred times the first. Like timber stacked for a long voyage, every extra hull demands disproportionately more wood, so a farm of ten thousand puppets faces a ruinous bill while one honest agent pays almost nothing. An onyx ledger records funding trails, so proxies split to dodge the price are caught by graph analysis and stripped of standing. Attack cost grows faster than attacker size.
